text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Seven opposition parties confirmed they would like to take part in the October 20 local polls but want the voting to be postponed, citing the lack of time needed to comply with their conditions.

- The centre-right Democratic Alliance Party is sending mixed and doubtful signals to its electorate by adopting two different lines of action ahead of the October 20 local polls, the paper said in a commentary.

- Parliament decided that members of the voting commissions who refuse to sign the return cards and quit the commission before the vote count has ended could be sentenced to three years in jail. The draft envisages a nine-year term.
- A 34-year-old Briton who admitted he had sexually abused two Albanian minors may get up to five years in jail.
- The opposition Socialist Party debates whether its candidate for mayor of Tirana will be a politician or the country's most famous basketball player.
- Doctors are alarmed at the spread of a polio outbreak in Albania which has affected 41 people.
- Tirana Bank, a Greek-owned bank, is expected to start operation in Tirana after receiving a licence by the central bank on Thursday. The bank plans to set up seven branches in other cities soon.
- Albanian central bank governor Kristaq Luniku says the privatisation of the banking system will end by the year 2000.
- The fifth private television station started broadcasting in Albania amid a lack of legislation regulating their activities. Parliament is in a quandary whether to shut them down or legalise them.
- Albanian law on sexual abuser of minors is too soft and the latest cases of paedophilia should prompt tougher laws.
- Four cases with explosives have been stolen from a military depot in the southern town of Vlora.
- An official of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development has promised Albania the bank will deliver within this year financing for an important road corridor.
